subject: SIG addendum for air-gapped deployment — artifact transfer, update cadence, support model
messages:
From: Sarah Dunn <sarah.dunn@acme.bio>
To: connor_obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Biotech Security <sec@acme.bio>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 15:23:00 -0400
Subject: SIG addendum for air-gapped deployment — delivery & support

Hi Connor,

Thanks for the demo last week. As we move toward an evaluation in our air-gapped environment, our procurement and security teams requested a SIG addendum that specifically covers:

- Mechanisms for delivering artifacts (models, runtime binaries, hotfixes) to an air-gapped site
- Expected cadence for updates/patches and how offline updates are validated
- Chain-of-custody and proof-of-delivery expectations for physical media
- Support model for incident response when systems are not network-connected
- Evidence we can rely on for SOC 2/SIG requests (scan results, signed manifests, build provenance)

I've attached our baseline SIG request PDF and highlighted the air-gap sections. Can Redwood provide a short addendum plus a runbook for artifact delivery and an example chain-of-custody? Also need to understand if a remote read-only agent is required and any customer responsibilities.

Target timeline: pilot delivery week of Aug 16th.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Dunn
Head of Security
Acme Biotech
[Attachment: ACME_SIG_Request_20260730.pdf (PDF)]
From: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: SIG addendum for air-gapped deployment — delivery & support

Folks — forwarding Sarah's request from Acme. Key asks below.

Proposed approach (high level):
- Provide a one-page SIG addendum that references the SIG baseline and adds air-gap-specific controls (artifact transfer, manual update window, signed manifests).
- Two artifact delivery options: 1) Encrypted, signed USB (agentless) shipped by courier + signed manifest; 2) Onsite handoff with our field engineer and witnessed chain-of-custody (higher cost).
- Offline update cadence: quarterly scheduled updates + unscheduled security hotfix window (24–72h SLA for critical CVEs with courier/patch dispatch).
- Evidence package: signed build manifest (SHA256), SBOM, ephemeral audit report (screenshot of signed build pipeline), and SOC 2 relevant extracts.
- Support model: define remote triage (email/phone) + scheduled on-site windows. For Dedicated/Private customers we can include a paid support addendum with guaranteed on-site windows.

I'll draft the addendum and an internal checklist. Marissa, can you validate if the SOC 2 artifacts we usually hand over are sufficient or if security needs anything additional for chain of custody?

Thanks,
Connor
Connor Obrien
Sr. Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: airgap_evidence_checklist.xlsx (XLSX)]
From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 01 Aug 2026 08:17:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Fwd: SIG addendum for air-gapped deployment — delivery & support

Adding some operational detail for the draft: 

- Artifact packaging: we deliver signed tarballs + detached signature file (.sig) and an accompanying signing certificate. For larger model binaries we provide an encrypted archive split across multiple media if needed.
- Validation at customer site: local validation script that checks signature and checksum; we'll provide the script and instructions.
- Update mechanism: 'secure-update-runner' — a self-contained binary customers can run locally to apply updates. It does not phone home; it validates signatures against our public key and applies artifacts.
- Emergency hotfix: if a critical vulnerability is found, we prepare a signed hotfix and dispatch via priority courier; customer can opt for on-site installation by our engineer (SOW).
- Costing: courier fees + optional on-site engineer day rates; recurring quarterly update bundles (optional subscription).

I'll attach a chain-of-custody template and an example manifest for reference.

- Dev
Dev Patel
Platform Ops

From: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>

Cc: Acme Biotech Security <sec@acme.bio>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2026 08:32:00 -0400
Subject: SIG addendum draft for air-gapped deployment — attached

Hi Sarah,

Thanks — attached is our initial draft addendum and an example checklist for artifact delivery. The addendum covers:

- Acceptable delivery methods (encrypted signed media, escorted handoff)
- Signed manifest and SHA256 checksum requirements
- Update cadence (quarterly + emergency hotfixes) and validation steps using our secure-update-runner
- Support tiers and response windows (email triage, phone escalation, optional on-site SOW)
- Evidence package contents we can provide to satisfy SIG / SOC 2 reviewers

A couple of clarifications we need from you to finalize the document:
1) Do you require on-site witness for every update or only for initial model delivery?
2) Is Acme able to run the local validation script, or would you prefer we run it on-site?
3) Any specific chain-of-custody form your procurement team requires (we included a generic template).

If you agree with the approach we can DocuSign the addendum and schedule a pilot drop week of Aug 16th.

Best,
Connor
Sr. Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_airgap_addendum_draft_v1.pdf (PDF)]
From: Sarah Dunn <sarah.dunn@acme.bio>
To: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Biotech Security <sec@acme.bio>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2026 09:41:00 -0400
Subject: Re: SIG addendum draft for air-gapped deployment — attached

Connor,

Thanks for the quick turnaround — this looks promising. A few follow-ups from the security and procurement teams:

- Proof-of-delivery: we prefer a signed manifest plus courier tracking record for each shipment. For initial model delivery we'll require a witnessed handoff; quarterly updates can be couriered with signed manifest.
- On-site validation: we'll run the local validation script for couriered updates. For any hotfix where we request Redwood on-site, procurement will require a statement of work and travel lead times.
- Chain-of-custody: your template is fine — procurement will add their PO number once we sign.

Next steps: please send the DocuSign link and an example SOW for on-site engineer support. Once we have those Procurement will start the PO process. Pilot week of Aug 16th still works.

Cheers,
Sarah
Head of Security, Acme Biotech
